title: Electricity: Magnetic and Heating Effects
seo_title: Electricity Class 8 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 4)
short_title: magnetic and heating effects of current
standard_text: Magnetic effect of electric current; electromagnets and how to make them stronger; uses of electromagnets such as the electric bell and cranes; heating effect of current and its uses; fuses, MCBs and electrical safety; energy-efficient lighting (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 4).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 8 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 4: the magnetic effect of current, electromagnets, the electric bell, the heating effect, heaters and fuses, MCBs and electrical safety. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Current makes a wire hot and makes a coil a magnet.
key_sub: More turns or more current: a stronger electromagnet.
body_html:
How to think about it

A wire carrying current behaves like a magnet and deflects a compass. A coil of insulated wire wound on a soft iron core becomes an electromagnet when current flows; it is stronger with more turns or more current, and its poles reverse when the current reverses. Electric bells, scrapyard cranes, motors and loudspeakers use electromagnets.

Current also heats a wire. Heaters, irons and kettles use nichrome elements. A fuse has a thin wire that melts if the current is too large; an MCB switches off automatically. Avoid overloading sockets and use ISI-marked appliances.

Example

Coil A: 50 turns; coil B: 100 turns; same current. Stronger?

more turns

Answer: coil B

Example

Why does a fuse wire melt?

too much current heats it

Answer: it protects the circuit

Common mistakes

  • Thinking an electromagnet stays magnetic after switching off.
  • Using a thick copper wire as a fuse.
  • Thinking heating is the only effect of current.
